beautiful place, but nothing ever grows there winter time: clocks go back by one hour this weekend. seasons of grief: while grief , like weather , will always be in our lives, our experience of it is always changing. just when the heat of summer feels like too much or the arrival of fall weather makes you long for the freedom of summer or the dark winter days feel heavy or the spring rains keep you shut in, a new season arrives to reminds you that things always change. so too will your relationship with your grief. thank the earth: in gratefulness we thank the earth, for the many blessing she can birth. we need to treat her with respect for so many things we now expect. with hopeful hearts we plant a seed, carefully tending to its need. kissed by the sun and watered with care, a sprout breaks through to greet the air. as a precious plant is born to earth, thank motor natur for its birth. you’ll reap the harvest of dreams come true as the seed you nurtured with nurture you. short but sweet : after starting a new diet, rose altered her drive to town to avoid passing her favourite bakery. rose accidentally drove by the bakery this morning and there in the window were a host of her favourite goodies. rose felt this was no accident, so she prayed, “lord, it’s up to you. if you want me to have any of those delicious goodies, create a parking place for me directly in front of the bakery. ” and sure enough, he answered her prayer. on the eighth time around the street, there it was! some thoughts for the week: “learn character from trees, values from roots, and change from leaves. ” tasneem hameed “what if, today we were grateful for everything? ” charlie brown “every day we are given chances to be a little wiser than before. ” sonia choquette “in every person who comes near you, look for what is good and strong. ” john ruskin “should we feel at times disheartened and discouraged, a simple movement of heart to- ward god will renew our powers. whatever he may demand of us, he will give us at the moment the strength and courage that we need. ” françois fénelon “forgiveness is a funny thing—it warms the heart and cools the sting. ” william ward “the true test of civilization is not the census, nor the size of the cities, nor the crops — no, but the kind of man the country turns out. ” ralph emerson “if i could hear christ praying for me in the next room, i would not fear a million enemies. yet distance makes no difference. he is praying for me. ” robert mccheyne “i took a walk in the woods and came out taller than the trees. ” henry thoreau “we are not here to play, to dream, to drift. we have hard work to do and loads to lift. shun not the battle; face it.’tis god’s gift. ” maltbie babcock “we need deliberately to call to mind the joys of our journey. perhaps we should try to write down the blessings of one day. we might begin; we could never end; there are not pens or paper enough in all the world. ” george buttrick “from heaven even the most miserable life will look like one bad night at an inconvenient hotel. ” teresa of ávila newmarket & taur

(thursday morning mass is cancelled that day). the autumn station mass at analeentha church will be at the 9.30am mass on friday 30th october. remembrance mass for those who died during the year will take place on friday, 13th november, 7.30pm at the church of st john the baptist, burnfort. november indulgences for the holy souls praying for the faithful departed who are in purgatory is a traditional feature of the church’s life. the month of november is the month when this is emphasised most of all. in the first week of november plenary (full) indulgences may be gained for the holy souls. indu lgences are the remission before god of the temporal punishment due to sins whose guilt has already been forg iven. the faithful christian who is duly disposed gains the indulgence under prescribed conditions for either himself of the departed. indulgences are granted through the ministry of the church which, as the dispenser of the grace of redemption, distributes the treasury of the merits of christ and the saints. ind ulgences for the holy souls may be gained in one of the following ways: 1. from 12 o’clock noon on 1 november until midnight on 2 nove mber, all who have confessed, received holy communion and prayed for the pope’s intentions (one our father and hail mary) can gain one plenary (full) indulgence for the dead by visiting a ch urch, and there reciting one our father and the apostle’s creed. confession may be made at any time within the week preceding or the week following 1 november. holy communion may be received on any day from 1 november to 8 november. 2. the faithful who visit a cemetery and pray for the dead may gain a plenary indulgence applicable only to the holy souls once per day every day of november. the conditions mentioned above apply also for this. cemetery prayers in november st. gobnait’s; sunday 1st nov. at 3.00 p.m.(if weather prohibits, prayers will be said in st. mary’s church at 3st. joseph’s ; sunday 8th nov. at 3.00 p.m . monday is the feast of all souls . a plenary indulgence will apply for the 1st & 2nd november and also from the 1st to the 8th november. plenary indulgence the church offers a plenary indulgence during these days for those who have died and who are awaiting purification – we refer to these as souls in purgatory. a plenary indulgence is a remission of the punishment due to s ins and is gained by our prayers for the dead. it may be gained in two ways: 1. once by visiting a church between midday november 1st and midnight november 2nd and there say one our father and the apostles creed and also pray the pope’s intentions. 2. once each day by visiting a cemetery from midday november 1st to november 8th and praying for the dead. both these indulgences require that the sacraments of holy communion and reconciliation be received within twenty days. remembering our dead all souls’ day invites us to pause, remember and reflect, not with fear or despair, but with hope and love. it is a quiet sacred time in the christian calen dar when we turn our hearts toward those who have gone before us. it reminds us that death is not an end, but a rite of passage and that love, especially in christ, does not end at the grave. we remember the ordinary faithful, our parents, friends, neighbours, strangers who lived, struggled and hoped just like we do. some may have died suddenly, others after long goodbyes. some we knew intimately; others we never met. yet we are all connected in the mystery of the communion of saints, the living, the dead, and those yet to come. on this day, we pray for the souls in purgatory, trusting that our prayers, united with the mercy of god, help them on their journ ey towards full union with him. our prayers are acts of love, and reminders that they are not for gotten. all souls’ day gently confronts us with our own mortality. but instead o f leading us to fear, it calls us to live well with compassion, humility, forgiveness, and faith so that when our time comes, we too may be welcomed into the fullness of god's presence. prayer on visiting the grave of a loved one father in heaven, as we stand before the resting place of our beloved , we remember the gift they were and continue to be to each of us here present. we thank you for their life, the love they shared with us, and we pray that they are with you now, enjo ying the fullness of eternal life. comfort us in our sadness, strengthen us with your hope, until we are united with them again in the love of christ and we are with you and our loved one forever. amen. cemetery prayers sunday 1st november - prayers will be offered in st. fanahan’s cemetery adjoining the parish church immediately after the 11.30am mass and at brigown cemetery at 2.30pm. sunday 8th november - prayers will be offered in the presentation convent cemetery immediately after the 11.30am mass and in marshalstown cemetery at 2.30pm.

exploring the merging of diocese in the province of cashel at the request of the holy see, the bishops of irel and have been considering how our diocesan structures best serve our shared mission in the years ahead. this is not simply a question of boundaries, admini strative adjustments or the sharing of resources more effectively. primarily it is about we can better proclaim the gospel, support our clergy, relig ious and lay people, and strengthen our parishes and communities for evangelisation. as part of this discernment, the bishops of the cashel province considered a range of possible configurations. the following options are presented for further ref lection and consultation across the seven dioceses of the cashel province. 1. archdiocese of cashel and emly and diocese of limer ick merge. 2. archdiocese of cashel & emly, diocese of limerick a nd diocese of killaloe merge. 3. archdiocese of cashel and emly and waterford and lismore merge. 4. diocese of limerick and diocese of killaloe merge. 5. diocese of limerick and diocese of cloyne merge. 6. diocese of cork and ross and diocese of cloyne merge. 7. diocese of cloyne and the diocese of waterford and lismore merge. 8. diocese of kerry and diocese of limerick merge. 9. diocese of kerry and diocese of cloyne merge. 10. diocese of kerry and the diocese of cork and ross m erge. maintain the current diocesan structures – ruled out by the papal nuncio! these are not decisions or an agreed map f or the future, rather material for further discussion. as bishops, we recognise that dioceses are communities of faith with their own histories, relationships and traditions. any change must therefore be approached with prayer, sensitivity and care for the people and communities involved. synodal discernment also asks each of us to look be yond our own self-interests and to consider what will best serve the catholic church i n ireland and in particular munster as a whole. everyone in every parish is encourag ed to make their voice heard when opportunities for consultation are announced locally by their diocesan bishop. finally, we encourage everyone to actively engage i n this process, and to the keep this central question at the heart our prayer and reflec tion: how can we best equip the catholic church in munste r for mission, evangelisation and the service of god’s people? with every blessing, bishops of munster province world missions sunday : thank you for your support of mission sunday. if have notd onated before and you wish to do so or you may either donate over the phone (01) 497 2035 or on our website:

mitchel stown paris h & com munity newsletter volume : 16 issue : 31 date: 24th & 25th october 2026 thirtieth sunday in ordinary time thought for the day legalist or lover what’s the difference between a legalist and a lover? the le galist keeps score, the lover doesn’t. love thinks of how it might give more, do more, dem onstrate love more fully. there are many examples of people who are poor in pocket, but rich in love. more than anything else, god wants to be in a love relationship with you (gospel). he wants your love more than your obedience or service! but if love god, you will do those other things. so, are you a legalist or a lover, alive or dead in how you live your faith? matthew 22:34-40 when the pharisees heard that jesus had silenced the sadducees they got together and, to disconcert him , one of them put a question, ‘master, which is the greatest commandment of the law?’ jesus said, ‘you must love the lord your god with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind. this is the greatest and the first commandment. the second r esembles it: you must love your neighbour as yourself. on these two commandments hang the whole law, and the prophets also .’.’ responsorial psalm . 17(18):2-4,47,51 i love you, lord, my strength. “you must love’” another group from the leadership of the jews seek to catch jesus out, the sadducees. jesus answers their question correctly by saying th at love of god comes before all else, how ever he also adds the second commandment, love your neig hbour as yourself. in this way jesus is telling us that to love god is to love one another. we cannot separate them. "if anyone says , 'i love god,' and yet hates his brother or sister, is a liar. for the person who does not love his brothe r or sister whom he has seen cannot love god whom he has not seen.". (1john 4:20). this love is not to be just words or mere talk but to be practical as we hear in the first reading for this sunday from the book of exodus. “ you must not molest the stranger or oppress him, you lived as strangers in the land of egypt. you must not be harsh with the widow, or with the orphan ” (ex22:20) memory is a very important part of our lives, it is important to recall who we are and where we come from. to love the stranger for the israelites is to remember that they were strangers in othe r lands in the past, and they know what it is not to belong. god has called us all into his family, we belong to him. while we can all be comfortable in belonging to a particular people and place and be wary of strangers, of people different to ourselves w hich can lead to segregation, racism, blaming stranger for everything, we as christians know that we are up of people from every nation and culture. our belonging is in christ and thus we are called to love one another as jesus loves us. welcoming to the stranger and to those in need. carrigtwohill

saints feast days for the coming week wednesday, 28th october - simon & jude: the teaching of the apostles is the living gospel for all to hear. their authority comes from their fidelity to christ and his message. st. jude i s the patron saint of useless causes. thursday, 29th october – st. colman : he hailed from kilmacduagh, co. galway. son of a chieftain named duagh. hermit in arranmore where he built two churches. his reputation for holiness attracted too much attention, so he retreated to the woods of burren in 592 to live in isolation. in 610, on land donated by king guaire of connacht , he founded a monastery which became the center of the diocese of kilmacduagh . he reluctantly served as the house’s first abbot, the dioceses first bishop. saturday, 31st october - blessed dominic collins: was born around 1566 in the town of youghal, co cork. in 1598, after a military career, he entered the society of jesus as a brother. he returned to ireland in 1601, but on the 16th june 1602, was captured by the english who tried in vain to make him abjure his faith. condemned to death, he was hanged in his native town on 31st october 1602. sunday, 1st november - all saints: ‘the ultimate object of veneration of the saints is the glory of god and the sanctification of humanity by conforming one’s life fully to the divine will and by imitating the virtue of those who were pre- existent disciples of the lord.’ monday, 2nd november - all souls: ‘indeed the church in its pilgrim members, from the very earliest days of the christian faith, has honoured with great res pect the memory of the dead; and ‘because it is a holy and a wholesome thought to pray for the dead that they may be loosed from thei r sins.’ (2 mac: 12-46), she offers her suffrages for them. these consist, primarily, in the celebration of the eucharist, and prayers for the dead, alms , deeds, works of mercy, and the application of indulgences to the souls of the faithful departed’. all saints we can often get side-tracked by canonised saints a nd forget the saints that we, ourselves, have known. these were people who did the ‘ordinary’ ext raordinarily well; who brought us untold joy by simply being, caring, loving, by lives poured in the service of others. they were people who loved life, who made us laugh and laughed themselves till their sides hurt; who affirmed us and others; who built up rather than tore down; they also thought of the world as essentially a good place and rejoiced in it, while being fully aw are of their own shortcomings. thomas merton once wrote: ‘forme, to be a saint is to be myself. ’ masses during the week in the parish church – 26th to 30th october 2026 monday (bank holiday): mass: 11am tuesday to friday: rosary: 9:30am mass: 10am friday: divine mercy: 3pm. confessions 31st october 2026 confessions in parish church: saturday 12 noon parish masses on sunday 1st november 2026 – feast of all saints parish church – vigil 7:30pm; 8:30am and 11:30am. killacluig; – 10:00am. please note mass times are displayed on church noticeboards. live streaming of masses in the parish church, please use the following link:
